messages.subject: time series plot
parts:
Hi, I am trying to produce plots of time series data, a few rows are shown below:

There are 10,000 rows, each representing a city and all months since 1998-01 to 2013-9:

RegionName State Metro CountyName 1998-01 1998-02 1998-03
New York NY New York Queens 1.3414 1.344 1.3514
Los Angeles CA Los Angeles Los Angeles 12.8841 12.5466 12.2737
Philadelphia PA Philadelphia Philadelphia 1.626 0.5639 0.2414
Phoenix AZ Phoenix Maricopa 2.7046 2.5525 2.3472

I want to produce a plot by Metro, X axis would be the months (1998-01, 1998-02, etc) and the Y axis would be values for each Metro for that month.  

Here is my code: 

forecl <- read.csv("Foreclosure.csv", header = T)

foreclt <- melt(forecl, id=c("RegionName", "State", "Metro", "CountyName" )) 

foreclt$RegionName <-NULL

foreclt$State <-NULL

foreclt$CountyName <-NULL 

ggplot(foreclt, aes(x = variable, y = value, colour = variable))

Error: No layers in plot

Please help me with this error;

Also how can I selectively print graphs for specific Metro?  Thank you very much.

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: time series plot
parts:
You need to add a geom_* in order to actually see a plot. 

For example:
ggplot(foreclt, aes(x = variable, y = value, colour = variable)) + geom_point()

If it's time series, you might want to add a line, but your example isn't reproducible so I'm not sure which which grouping factor you will need. 
?geom_line()

If you want to look at data from different Metro areas you could consider faceting by Metro
+ facet_wrap(.~Metro)

Or you can subset your data and then plot each metro individually. 
?subset

HTH, 

Brandon
